Switching from Windows to Mac doesn't actually come with that many software limitations. Not only can the platform run most major computer applications, there are also plenty of exclusive and useful Mac apps to choose from.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, the latest testing shows that, whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games running on Mac have reached their best performance ever...

Apple has its own exclusive game porting toolkit to help developers assess how their Windows games will run on Mac, aiming to encourage and facilitate game ports to the Mac platform.

However, as Macworld's Filipe Esposito noted, this toolkit is also being used by gamers to unofficially run Windows software on Mac—he himself is one of them. He pointed out that the latest test version brings significant performance improvements, using GTA V as an example.

After testing the game porting toolkit 4 beta for several days on a MacBook Pro equipped with an M4 Pro chip, he found that the performance improvements essentially transformed the experience of running demanding Windows games... On the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, using the same game settings and benchmarks, GTA V's frame rate jumped from approximately 106 fps in the GPTK 3 era to approximately 176 fps in the GPTK 4 beta—an increase of about 66%. The game ran quite smoothly at 2K resolution with medium-to-high graphics settings.

He acknowledged that not every game will see such dramatic improvements, but still hopes these advances will encourage game developers to consider Mac as a viable platform.
